security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel (HS-mode), when bhyve writes vsatp.MODE=Bare for a guest VM via vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs() at vmm_riscv.c:176, or when the kernel clears menvcfg.SSE, the Sspmpss extension deactivates: all XWR=010 SPMP entries revert to reserved encodings, so shadow-stack instructions that were previously permitted against those regions instead raise guest-page faults (VS/VU) or access faults (S/U). Conversely, if the kernel sets menvcfg.SSE without properly initializing SPMP shadow-stack entries, existing XWR=010 encodings become live with no shadow-stack memory carved out, silently allowing shadow-stack instructions to write to arbitrary memory through any SPMP entry that happens to decode as XWR=010.
security_spec.summary: Sspmpss shadow-stack SPMP enforcement gates on satp.MODE!=Bare and menvcfg.SSE, both writable by FreeBSD's HS-mode kernel; bhyve's vsatp writes and any menvcfg manipulation can silently deactivate or misconfigure shadow-stack protection, turning CFI-guaranteed faults into unintended access grants or legitimate accesses into spurious faults
